subject: AI
title: AI Fundamentals Notes
description: Original beginner notes on AI meaning, examples, data, model learning, and responsible AI use.
content:
Meaning of AI:
Artificial Intelligence is the ability of a computer system to perform tasks that normally need human-like thinking, such as recognising speech, finding patterns, suggesting routes, or classifying images.

Daily Life Examples:
- Voice assistants answer simple questions.
- Maps suggest routes using traffic information.
- Email systems detect spam messages.
- Shopping apps recommend products based on past activity.

Role of Data:
Data helps AI systems learn patterns. Clean and relevant data improves results. Incomplete or unfair data can produce poor output.

Responsible Use:
AI should support people, protect privacy, and avoid unfair decisions. A student should not blindly trust automated answers without checking them.

Quick Practice:
Write three places where you have seen AI-like suggestions. For each, mention what data the system may be using.

subject: AI
title: CBSE Class 9 AI Employability Skills Notes
description: Original revision notes covering ICT, self-management, communication, and entrepreneurial skills for CBSE Class 9 AI learners.
content:
How to use these notes:
Read one topic at a time. After each topic, write two examples from your own school or home life.

ICT and Its Impact:
ICT means Information and Communication Technology. It includes computers, smartphones, internet, email, video meetings, online learning platforms, digital payments, and other tools used to create, store, process, and share information.
- ICT helps students learn through videos, notes, quizzes, and online classes.
- ICT helps offices keep records, prepare reports, and communicate quickly.
- ICT helps citizens use services such as online forms, bill payments, and digital certificates.

Cyber Safety:
Cyber safety means using digital devices and the internet carefully. Students should avoid unknown links, protect passwords, log out from shared devices, and think before posting anything online. A strong password should be unique and should not contain personal details such as date of birth or mobile number.

Self-Management Skills:
Self-management is the ability to guide your thoughts, behaviour, time, and habits responsibly. A self-managed student comes prepared, completes work on time, asks for help when needed, and learns from feedback.
- Self-awareness means knowing your strengths and areas for improvement.
- Self-confidence means trusting your ability while still being ready to learn.
- Time management means planning tasks so important work is completed first.
- Goal setting means deciding a clear target and working step by step.

Communication Skills:
Communication is the process of sharing ideas, information, and feelings clearly. It can be verbal, non-verbal, written, or visual. Good communication requires listening, polite language, suitable body language, and clear feedback.

Entrepreneurial Skills:
An entrepreneur identifies a need, plans a useful solution, manages resources, and takes responsible risks. Entrepreneurial thinking is useful even for students because it builds creativity, problem solving, planning, teamwork, and confidence.

Quick Revision:
- ICT connects people and information.
- Cyber safety protects devices, accounts, and privacy.
- Self-management builds discipline and confidence.
- Communication improves understanding and teamwork.
- Entrepreneurial skills help convert ideas into useful action.

subject: IT
title: Presentation Basics Notes
description: Original notes for making clear slides, using visuals wisely, and presenting confidently.
content:
Purpose of a Presentation:
A presentation explains information to an audience using slides, visuals, and speech. It is useful for school projects, awareness topics, reports, and demonstrations.

Slide Design:
- Keep one main idea on each slide.
- Use short points instead of long paragraphs.
- Choose readable fonts and clear contrast.
- Align text and images neatly.
- Use consistent colours.

Images and Charts:
Images should support the message. A chart is useful when numbers need comparison. Every image or chart should be easy to understand.

Delivery Tips:
Speak clearly, face the audience, practise before presenting, and avoid reading every word from the screen.

Quick Practice:
Create a five-slide outline on cyber safety: title, problem, safe habits, example, and conclusion.

subject: IT
title: CBSE Class 9 IT Digital Skills Notes
description: Original notes for ICT basics, digital documentation, spreadsheet basics, cyber safety, and responsible computer use.
content:
ICT Basics:
ICT is the use of digital tools to handle information and communication. A computer accepts input, processes data, stores it, and produces output. Input devices include keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, and webcam. Output devices include monitor, printer, speakers, and projector.

Digital Documentation:
A digital document is a file created using a word processor. It may include text, headings, lists, tables, images, and page settings. A good document has a clear title, readable font, proper spacing, useful headings, and correct spelling.

Formatting Tips:
- Use bold text only for important words or headings.
- Keep font size consistent in body paragraphs.
- Use bullets for lists and numbering for steps.
- Insert tables when information must be compared.
- Preview before printing.

Spreadsheet Basics:
A spreadsheet arranges data in rows and columns. A cell is the box formed by a row and column. Formulas help calculate totals, averages, and other results. Charts help display data visually.

Cyber Safety:
Use strong passwords, avoid suspicious downloads, do not share OTPs, and log out from public computers. Digital footprints can affect future opportunities, so online behaviour should be respectful and careful.

Quick Revision:
- Hardware can be touched; software gives instructions.
- A document should be clear, consistent, and readable.
- A spreadsheet is useful for calculations and data analysis.
- Safe internet habits protect identity and data.

subject: AI
title: AI Project Cycle Notes
description: Original notes on problem scoping, data acquisition, data exploration, modelling, evaluation, and responsible deployment.
content:
Problem Scoping:
Problem scoping defines what issue will be solved, who is affected, why it matters, and how success will be measured.

Data Acquisition:
This step collects useful data from suitable sources. Data should be relevant, accurate, and collected responsibly.

Data Exploration:
Data exploration studies the data using summaries, tables, and charts. It helps find missing values, unusual entries, and useful patterns.

Modelling:
A model learns patterns from data and tries to make predictions or classifications. The model must be tested before use.

Evaluation:
Evaluation checks whether the model performs well. Accuracy, fairness, safety, and usefulness should all be considered.

Responsible Deployment:
When an AI solution is used, it should be monitored and improved with feedback.

subject: AI
title: CBSE Class 10 AI Employability Skills Notes
description: Original CBSE Class 10 AI notes covering communication, self-management, ICT, entrepreneurship, green skills, and AI project thinking.
content:
Communication Skills-II:
Effective communication shares information clearly and respectfully. Feedback should be specific, polite, and useful. Barriers such as noise, unclear language, assumptions, and poor listening can reduce understanding.

Self-Management Skills-II:
Self-management includes stress management, self-awareness, self-motivation, goal setting, planning, and responsible independent work. A good plan breaks a large task into small steps and checks progress regularly.

ICT Skills-II:
ICT skills include working with an operating system, managing files and folders, caring for devices, protecting against viruses, and using digital tools responsibly. Organised folders and meaningful file names save time.

Entrepreneurial Skills-II:
Entrepreneurs solve problems by identifying needs, planning solutions, understanding customers, managing resources, and learning from feedback. Responsible entrepreneurship balances profit with quality, honesty, and service.

Green Skills-II:
Green skills support sustainable living. They include saving electricity, reducing waste, reusing materials, conserving water, and choosing environment-friendly practices. Green jobs are work opportunities that protect or restore the environment.

AI Project Thinking:
An AI project begins with a clear problem. It needs relevant data, careful modelling, testing, evaluation, and responsible use. A useful AI solution should be accurate, fair, safe, and understandable.

Quick Revision:
- Communicate clearly and listen actively.
- Manage stress with planning and healthy routines.
- Keep files organised and devices secure.
- Think like an entrepreneur: observe, plan, act, improve.
- Use technology in a way that supports people and the environment.

subject: IT
title: Digital Skills Portfolio Notes
description: Original notes on organising practical IT evidence, screenshots, reflections, files, and review checklists.
content:
Digital Portfolio:
A digital portfolio is an organised collection of practical work. It shows what a learner can create and explain.

Useful Evidence:
- Final document files.
- Spreadsheet screenshots and charts.
- Database tables, forms, and reports.
- Web security notes and safe browsing examples.
- Short reflections explaining what was learned.

File Organisation:
Create a main folder and use subfolders for each module. Use clear file names such as spreadsheet-marksheet-v1 or dbms-library-report.

Reflection:
Reflection explains what was done, what was difficult, and how the work improved. It helps students understand their learning process.

Review Checklist:
Check that every file opens, screenshots are readable, personal data is protected, and work is explained in your own words.

subject: IT
title: CBSE Class 10 IT Advanced Skills Notes
description: Original notes for advanced documentation, spreadsheets, databases, web applications, and digital security.
content:
Digital Documentation (Advanced):
Advanced documentation uses styles, images, templates, tables of contents, and mail merge. Styles keep headings and paragraphs consistent. Templates save time when the same document format is used repeatedly. Mail merge creates personalised letters, labels, and certificates from one main document and a data source.

Electronic Spreadsheets (Advanced):
Advanced spreadsheets use formulas, functions, cell references, sorting, filtering, charts, and validation. Use absolute references when one fixed value must be used in many formulas. Review formulas before copying them across a large table.

Database Management System:
A database stores related data in an organised form. Tables contain records and fields. A primary key uniquely identifies each record. Queries retrieve selected data. Forms help with data entry, and reports present information clearly.

Web Applications and Security:
Web applications run through a browser. Examples include email, online forms, cloud documents, digital payments, and e-learning platforms. Security is important because online accounts and personal data can be misused.

Safe Digital Practices:
- Use strong, unique passwords.
- Avoid suspicious links and unknown downloads.
- Check website addresses carefully.
- Log out from shared devices.
- Back up important files.
- Share personal information only when necessary.

Quick Revision:
- Styles create consistent documents.
- Spreadsheets calculate and analyse data.
- Databases organise related records.
- Web applications need secure and responsible use.

subject: Python 083
title: Variables, Data Types and Operators Notes
description: Essential quick revision notes on Python tokens, mutable vs immutable types, arithmetic/logical operators, and basic input/output statements.
content:
Python Variables and Dynamic Typing:
In Python, variables are created when you assign a value to them. Variables hold references to objects, not actual values. Types are verified at runtime (dynamic typing).

Data Types:
- Numbers: int, float, complex
- Sequences: str, list, tuple
- Mappings: dict
- Sets: set

Mutable vs Immutable:
- Mutable (can change value): lists, dicts, sets
- Immutable (cannot change value): int, float, str, tuple

Operators:
- Arithmetic: +, -, *, /, //, %, **
- Logical: and, or, not
- Relational: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=

Revision Tip:
Remember that 5/2 returns 2.5 (float division) while 5//2 returns 2 (floor division) and 5%2 returns 1 (modulo/remainder).

subject: Python 083
title: Text File Handling and Operations Notes
description: Quick revision notes on opening, reading, writing, and appending files using open(), read(), readline(), and readlines() in Python.
content:
Opening a File:
Use the built-in open() function. Syntax: file_object = open(file_name, access_mode)
Access modes: 'r' (read), 'w' (write), 'a' (append), 'r+' (read & write).

Reading Methods:
- read(n): reads n bytes/characters. If no argument is passed, reads the entire file.
- readline(): reads a single line from the file as a string.
- readlines(): reads all lines and returns them as a list of strings.

Writing Methods:
- write(string): writes string to the file.
- writelines(list_of_strings): writes a list of strings to the file.

Always close files using file_object.close() to release system resources, or use the 'with' statement block for automatic closing:
with open('data.txt', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
